clue.text: Loss paid off in assignment

indicators.note: off suggests something gone wrong or out of order, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A financial loss gets written off in some assignment or accounting task.
explanation.walkthrough: 'paid off' reads as one phrase, but 'paid' belongs to the anagram fodder and 'off' alone signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Having something at your disposal means it is allocated to you, so the word is a synonym for allocation.

clue.text: Animal troop eviscerated eland, getting very full

parts.note: a pack is a group of wolves or dogs, a troop of animals

indicators.note: with its innards removed, the word keeps only its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A pack of predators guts an antelope and is left gorged.
explanation.definitionFit: A venue crammed to capacity is described as packed, an everyday synonym.

clue.text: See Irish artist in French department

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or see
an etcher is an artist who makes prints from engraved plates

explanation.surface: An instruction to go and look at an Irish painter's work somewhere in France.
explanation.definitionFit: Loir-et-Cher is an administrative region of central France, named after two rivers.

clue.text: Battle victim — may he just have seen the one that got him?

definitions.text: Battle victim — may he just have seen the one that got him?

parts.words: Battle victim — may he just have seen the one that got him?
parts.note: the English king killed at Hastings in 1066, by tradition shot in the eye by an arrow, so he may just have glimpsed it coming

explanation.surface: A wry question about a fallen soldier who perhaps spotted his killer.
explanation.walkthrough: The Bayeux Tapestry is often read as showing the king with an arrow in his eye, hence the joke about seeing the one that got him.
explanation.definitionFit: The last Anglo-Saxon king died at the Battle of Hastings, the most famous victim of that battle.

clue.text: Day drunken mate imprisons mate in tree

indicators.note: imprisons means holds inside, so one piece goes within the other
drunk means unsteady and jumbled, so the first word mate is rearranged

parts.note: a mate is a friend, a pal

explanation.surface: On some day a drunk friend locks up another friend in a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunken' turns the first 'mate' into ATEM, and 'imprisons' puts PAL inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The date palm is a tree grown for its sweet fruit, so the tree is an example.

clue.text: Low born idiot

parts.note: b is the abbreviation for born in genealogies
an ass is a fool or idiot

explanation.surface: An insult calling someone a lowborn fool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Low born' reads as one word for humble birth, but 'Low' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: In music the lowest voice or register is called bass, the opposite of treble.

clue.text: In holy place I do His work

definitions.text: In holy place I do His work

indicators.note: In tells us the following letter sits inside the church word

parts.note: a minster is a large church, a holy place

explanation.surface: A clergyman speaking: in church I carry out God's work.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: a clergyman in a church does God's work.
explanation.definitionFit: A clergyman serving in a church performs God's work for his congregation.

clue.text: Pub welcomes the one who washes

indicators.note: welcomes means takes in, so the word the goes inside

parts.note: a bar is a pub

explanation.surface: A pub is happy to let in someone who keeps clean.
explanation.walkthrough: The word the is the fodder, tucked inside the pub word.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone taking a bath, or swimming, is a bather.

clue.text: In an instant scoundrel gets a girlfriend

parts.note: taken as written
a mo, short for a moment, is an instant
a rat is a contemptible person, a scoundrel

explanation.surface: A rogue quickly finds himself a girlfriend.
explanation.definitionFit: An inamorata is a female lover, from the Italian for one in love.

clue.text: Manx beast shows inner personality

indicators.note: a Manx cat has no tail, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: an animal is a beast

explanation.surface: A creature from the Isle of Man reveals its true self.
explanation.walkthrough: The Isle of Man's Manx cat is famously tailless, a common crossword signal for dropping a last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: In Jungian psychology the anima is the inner self or soul of a person.

clue.text: Game that uses King and Queen after work's over

indicators.note: after places the royal letters behind the reversed work
over means turned over, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a work
K is the chess and card abbreviation for king
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

explanation.surface: A card game that uses kings and queens, played once the working day ends.
explanation.definitionFit: Poker is a card game of betting and bluffing.

clue.text: Labour challenger "hits women" — not true

indicators.note: not true means out of line or askew, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A denial that a Labour politician hits women.
explanation.walkthrough: Owen Smith challenged Jeremy Corbyn for the UK Labour Party leadership in 2016.
explanation.definitionFit: He was the Welsh MP who stood against the sitting leader for the party's leadership.

clue.text: Shortened see saw soothed

indicators.note: shortened means cut down, so the word see loses its last letter

parts.note: saw, as in was going out with, means dated

explanation.surface: A shortened seesaw calms someone down, like a gentle playground ride.
explanation.walkthrough: 'see saw' looks like the playground toy, but the two words work separately; 'saw' is in the sense of went out with someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone calmed with a drug, or simply settled, has been sedated, a synonym for soothed.

clue.text: Judge alligator's skin by similarly carnivorous animal?

indicators.note: the skin is the outside, so only the first and last letters of the reptile word are used

parts.note: a biter, like an alligator, is a creature that bites

explanation.surface: Judging an alligator hide alongside another meat-eater.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'alligator's' is a possessive: only the outside of 'alligator' gives AR.
explanation.definitionFit: An arbiter is someone who settles disputes, a judge or umpire.

clue.text: 50 in band with underworld goddess almost take on risky mission

indicators.note: in puts the numeral inside the band

parts.note: a belt is a band
L is the Roman numeral for 50

indicators.note: almost drops the last letter of the goddess's name

parts.note: Hecate is the Greek goddess of witchcraft and the underworld

explanation.surface: A goddess of the dead joins a group fifty strong on a dangerous venture.
explanation.walkthrough: In the fable the mice want a bell hung on the cat, but no mouse dares do it.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to undertake a perilous task for the common good.

clue.text: Meal for Parisian one inside 19 church

indicators.note: inside places the French word within the other letters

parts.note: the answer to 19 across means big, abbreviated L as on clothing labels
un is French for one

explanation.surface: A Parisian eats one meal in a big church.
explanation.definitionFit: Lunch is the midday meal.

clue.text: Say you know Brad Pitt? Pardon me, but that's ridiculous

indicators.note: ridiculous means absurd or crazy, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Someone claims to be pals with a film star and is met with disbelief.
explanation.definitionFit: To name-drop is to mention famous acquaintances casually to impress, as a question example shows.

clue.text: Beatles song from remixed White Album, as not black? Right

indicators.note: remixed, as a record is, means the letters are rearranged
not says the following letter is left out of the fodder

parts.note: B is the pencil abbreviation for black

explanation.surface: A Beatles track taken from a remixed White Album, played as something not black.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram is of WHITE ALBUM AS minus B (black), plus R. The song really is on Magical Mystery Tour, not the White Album.
explanation.definitionFit: This 1967 Lennon song is a well-known Beatles track.

clue.text: Girl after lollies to perform on frozen sheet?

indicators.note: after puts the girl's name behind the lollies

parts.note: ice lollies are ices
Kate is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl after ice lollies goes skating on ice.
explanation.definitionFit: To glide across ice on blades is to skate on a frozen surface, as the question mark allows.

clue.text: Big Guardian Deity emptied grave

parts.note: a Lar is a Roman household god, a guardian spirit

indicators.note: emptied means the inside letters are removed, leaving only the ends

explanation.surface: A huge guardian god digs up an emptied grave.
explanation.definitionFit: Large is a plain synonym for big in size.

clue.text: River to surge up, which involves constant worry

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon, England

indicators.note: involves means contains, so the constant letter goes inside

parts.note: to surge up is to rise
c is the symbol for a constant in mathematics, and for the speed of light

explanation.surface: A river swelling that brings with it ceaseless anxiety.
explanation.definitionFit: To exercise someone can mean to trouble or preoccupy them, so a synonym for worry.

clue.text: Deep regret about additional shilling invested

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: invested means placed within, so the coin letter goes inside

parts.note: more means additional or extra
s was the abbreviation for the old British shilling coin

explanation.surface: Bitter regret over having put another shilling into an investment.
explanation.definitionFit: Remorse is guilt and sorrow for a wrong done, deep regret.

clue.text: Churchman appears topless in couples counselling service

indicators.note: topless means losing the top, the first letter in a down clue

parts.note: a prelate is a senior clergyman

explanation.surface: A bishop shows up bare-chested at marriage guidance.
explanation.walkthrough: Relate is a UK charity offering relationship counselling.
explanation.definitionFit: The British relationship-guidance charity is called Relate, so the name of the service.

clue.text: Recital's tricky piece

indicators.note: tricky means involved or awkward, so the letters are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: A musician's recital includes a difficult piece.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'Recital's' stands for 'is', a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: An article is a piece of writing in a newspaper or magazine.

clue.text: Reply from lesbians we respect

indicators.note: from tells us the letters are taken out of the run of words that follow

explanation.surface: A response from a group of lesbian women we admire.
explanation.definitionFit: An answer is a reply to a question.

clue.text: Old soldiers company keen to stifle resistance

indicators.note: to stifle is to smother, so the keen word wraps around the next letter

parts.note: hot on something means keen
R is the physics symbol for resistance

explanation.surface: A firm eager to suppress opposition from veteran troops.
explanation.definitionFit: A cohort was a unit of a Roman legion, so a body of ancient soldiers.

clue.text: Penniless young men outside bookies

indicators.note: outside means the young men wrap around the penniless word

parts.note: lads are young men
broke means having no money

explanation.surface: Skint young lads loiter outside a betting shop.
explanation.walkthrough: Ladbrokes is a big chain of British betting shops.
explanation.definitionFit: The firm is one of the best-known high-street bookmakers in Britain.

clue.text: Right time to speak wildly

parts.note: an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: The ideal moment to rant freely.
explanation.definitionFit: To rage is to rant or talk furiously, a verb sense of speaking wildly.

clue.text: Moral system demands witches flayed and chopped to bits

indicators.note: chopped to bits means cut up and reassembled, so the remaining letters are rearranged
flayed means skinned, so the outer letters of the word are removed

explanation.surface: A code of conduct calls for witches to be skinned and hacked up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flayed' strips W and S from WITCHES, leaving ITCHE, which 'chopped to bits' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: An ethic is a set of moral principles, a moral code.

clue.text: Ton pig eats new leather strip

indicators.note: eats means takes in, so the new letter goes inside the pig

parts.note: a hog is a pig

explanation.surface: A huge pig gobbles up a new length of leather.
explanation.definitionFit: A thong is a narrow strip of leather used as a lace or strap.

clue.text: See 18
